doc.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Learning 'The Duke' and the album cover photo
summary: She talks about learning Brubeck's 'The Duke' and the jumping photo for her album cover.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Did this tune take a while to get a handle on?

Yes, it’s very hard. But I’ve always loved it instrumentally. It’s a tune called “The Duke” by Dave Brubeck. And I’ve just always loved it instrumentally. And then I found out that it had words. So yeah, I had to sing it, because I liked it so much. And so I did my best. It’s tough.
Nice, real nice. I like the picture with the old time microphone.
Yeah. That picture on that cover was — the actual sheet music for “I Saw Stars” looks just like that, but we stuck my picture in the little frame there.
In this one I was going to ask you how many jumps did it take before they got the —
Well let’s see, I’m trying to think, probably about fifteen or twenty.
Was this in front of one of those photographer’s things?

It was in front of a backdrop. And that whole pose was an afterthought. I had gone into the photographer saying oh I want this with the wind and the scarf flowing in the background and I had all these poses to look carefree. And the photographer at the end of the session said, “Well why don’t you just try jumping just for the fun of it?” So those were the ones that were used.
